caption: EnemyBullet × Enemy is off in the matrix, so the bullet passes through the other enemy without a broadphase test and only reports contact against the Player.
Physics runs every 0.02 s while frames arrive every ~7 ms at 144 fps: without interpolation the body holds a pose across several frames, with Interpolate it glides one step behind.
The Locomotion state is a 1D blend tree on Speed: as Speed moves from 0 to 6 the weight slides from Idle through Walk to Run.
Each timer tick dirties its Canvas; with one Canvas all 12 elements re-batch, with a nested Dynamic Canvas only its 3 do.
Every pointer event tests each Graphic with Raycast Target on; turning it off on decoration cuts 11 tests to the 3 buttons.
One text change in a nested layout walks up to the root layout group, which then recomputes every element below it.
The same 2048x2048 texture drawn to scale per format: RGBA32 costs 16 MB, ASTC 8x8 1 MB, and a mip chain adds about a third on top.
Texture T with no bundle of its own is copied into every bundle that references it; giving it a shared bundle leaves one copy that both depend on.
Each load raises the count and each Release lowers it; the bundle unloads only at zero, so one missing Release keeps it resident.
The lesson's phone capture to scale: the main thread finishes PlayerLoop in 6.1 ms and then waits on the GPU, which is busy for the whole 22 ms frame.
Over a soak test a phone with no headroom throttles from 16.7 to 25 ms per frame, while the same rise from an 11 ms budget stays under the 60 fps line.
Batches of 64 run on worker threads in parallel with main-thread work when Complete() comes late; calling it right after Schedule() turns that time into waiting.
